questions.question: Who among the following led the Indian delegation to attend the 56th Annual General Meeting of the Board of Governors of Asian Development Bank (ADB) along with Investor/ Bilateral and other associated meetings, in Incheon, the Republic of Korea, from 2 to 5 May 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nirmala Sitharaman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs, **Nirmala Sitharaman**, led the Indian delegation to the 56th Annual General Meeting of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) held in Incheon, Republic of Korea.
 
• The meetings took place from **2 to 5 May 2023**, addressing critical issues like sustainable development, regional cooperation, and global economic challenges.
 
• During the event, the Indian delegation participated in **investor meetings, bilateral discussions, and other associated engagements**.
 
• Nirmala Sitharaman emphasized India's commitment to achieving sustainable economic growth and highlighted the country's leadership in climate action initiatives.
 
• The **ADB Annual Meeting** serves as a platform for member countries to discuss development priorities and financial collaborations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asian Development Bank (ADB)**

 
 
• Established in **1966**, the ADB is a regional development bank headquartered in Manila, Philippines.
 
• Its primary goal is to foster economic growth and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region through loans, technical assistance, and grants.
 
• India is a founding member of the ADB and one of its largest beneficiaries in terms of financial assistance.
 
• The ADB focuses on areas such as infrastructure, poverty reduction, education, and climate change mitigation.
 
 
 
• **India's Climate Action Leadership**
 
 
• India has committed to achieving **Net Zero emissions by 2070** as part of its climate action strategy.
 
• Key initiatives include the **National Solar Mission**, promoting renewable energy and reducing reliance on fossil fuels.
 
• India launched the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** to foster global cooperation in solar energy development.
 
• Efforts are being made to align development goals with sustainability through programs such as **PM-KUSUM** and UJALA.
 
 
 
• **Significance of ADB Annual Meetings**
 
 
• ADB Annual Meetings provide a platform for member nations to discuss **global economic trends and challenges**.
 
• It allows member countries to present their **development priorities** and explore financial collaborations.
 
• The meetings are attended by policymakers, investors, and representatives from multilateral institutions.
 
• Key topics include **poverty alleviation, climate resilience, gender equality, and regional integration**.
 
 
 
• **Nirmala Sitharaman's Leadership**
 
 
• As India's Finance Minister, Nirmala Sitharaman has been instrumental in implementing progressive economic reforms.
 
• She has focused on initiatives such as **Atmanirbhar Bharat** to promote self-reliance and economic resilience.
 
• Under her leadership, India has taken significant steps to improve ease of doing business and attract foreign investments.
 
• Sitharaman has consistently represented India at various global forums, advocating for equitable development and financial stability.

questions.question: According to Article 51A of the Indian Constitution, it is the fundamental duty of every person to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and ____________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**integrity of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 51A is part of the Indian Constitution's **Fundamental Duties**, introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• It mandates every Indian citizen to **uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India**.
 
• The term "integrity" emphasizes the obligation to preserve India's territorial and cultural cohesion.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile Soviet Union and aim to promote a sense of **patriotism and discipline** among citizens.
 
• While Fundamental Duties are non-enforceable by law, they are considered a moral and ethical guideline for Indian citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**

 
 
• Known as the "Mini-Constitution," it introduced several changes, including the addition of Fundamental Duties under Article 51A.
 
• The amendment also added the words "socialist," "secular," and "integrity" to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• Located in Part IVA (Article 51A) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Initially, there were 10 duties, but the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, added the 11th duty related to education for children.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced in a court of law.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Sovereignty, Unity, and Integrity**
 
 
• **Sovereignty:** Refers to India's supreme authority to govern itself without external interference.
 
• **Unity:** Emphasizes the political and cultural oneness of India despite its diversity.
 
• **Integrity:** Relates to maintaining the nation's territorial wholeness and harmony among its people.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• They serve as a constant reminder to citizens about their moral responsibilities towards the nation.
 
• They complement the Fundamental Rights by ensuring a balance between individual rights and societal obligations.

questions.question: The process by which a water body gradually becomes enriched with nutrients and minerals, mainly phosphorus and nitrogen, leading to enormous growth of algae on the surface of the water, thus decreasing the amount of dissolved oxygen in the water is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eutrophication**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is the process by which a water body becomes enriched with nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, leading to excessive growth of algae.
 
• This phenomenon often results from **runoff of fertilizers, sewage, and industrial waste** into water bodies.
 
• The excessive algae growth, also called **algal bloom**, blocks sunlight penetration into the water.
 
• As algae die and decompose, the process consumes large amounts of **dissolved oxygen**, creating oxygen-depleted zones.
 
• Low oxygen levels (hypoxia) can lead to the death of aquatic organisms, disrupting the **ecosystem balance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biomagnification**: The process by which the concentration of toxins increases as they move up the food chain, affecting top predators most severely.
 
• **Hypoxia**: A condition where oxygen levels in water are too low to sustain aquatic life, often a result of eutrophication.
 
• **Bioaccumulation**: The accumulation of harmful substances, such as pesticides or heavy metals, in an organism over time.
 
• **Point and Non-Point Sources**: Nutrient pollution causing eutrophication can originate from point sources (e.g., factories) or non-point sources (e.g., agricultural runoff).
 
• **Dead Zones**: Areas in water bodies where oxygen levels are too low to support life, often caused by eutrophication. The Gulf of Mexico is a well-known example.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters was associated with the series of nine articles known as 'New Lamp for Old'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurobindo Ghose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Aurobindo Ghose wrote the series of nine articles titled **'New Lamp for Old'** during his time as a political activist and intellectual.
 
• The articles were published in the newspaper **'Induprakash'** in the late 19th century, advocating for a more assertive approach to India's independence struggle.
 
• Aurobindo criticized the moderate methods of the Indian National Congress and called for a more radical approach to achieve self-rule.
 
• 'New Lamp for Old' marked the beginning of Aurobindo's active involvement in India's freedom movement, showcasing his sharp political insight.
 
• These writings reflect Aurobindo's early revolutionary ideology before transitioning to a spiritual path in later years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Induprakash Newspaper:**

 
 
• It was a prominent English-Marathi newspaper based in Bombay, known for publishing reformist and nationalist content.
 
• Induprakash served as a platform for discussing socio-political issues during the British colonial era.
 
 
 
• **Moderates vs Extremists:**
 
 
• The Moderates within the Indian National Congress favored gradual reforms and dialogue with the British government.
 
• Extremists, including leaders like Aurobindo, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal, advocated for self-reliance and direct action.
 
 
 
• **Aurobindo Ghose's Transition:**
 
 
• After his active political career, Aurobindo transitioned to spirituality and established the **Aurobindo Ashram** in Pondicherry.
 
• He developed the concept of Integral Yoga, focusing on the evolution of human consciousness.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Aurobindo's early political writings, including 'New Lamp for Old,' continue to inspire scholars and historians studying India's freedom movement.
 
• His dual contribution to politics and spirituality makes him a unique figure in Indian history.

questions.question: The Buland Darwaza was the structure built by Akbar at which of the following places in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fatehpur Sikri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Buland Darwaza**, also known as the "Gate of Magnificence," was built by Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1575 AD.
 
• It is located at **Fatehpur Sikri**, a city near Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• The gateway was constructed to commemorate Akbar's victory over Gujarat in 1573 AD.
 
• With a height of approximately **54 meters**, it is one of the largest gateways in the world.
 
• The structure is an architectural masterpiece showcasing a blend of **Persian and Mughal architectural styles**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fatehpur Sikri**

 
 
• Fatehpur Sikri was founded by Akbar in 1571 and served as the Mughal capital for around 15 years.
 
• The city is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its historical and architectural importance.
 
• It includes several notable structures like the Jama Masjid, Tomb of Salim Chishti, and Panch Mahal.
 
• Fatehpur Sikri is considered a masterpiece of Mughal architecture, reflecting the empire's grandeur and cultural advancements.
 
 
 
• **Akbar’s Architectural Contributions**
 
 
• Akbar extensively promoted Indo-Islamic architecture, blending Persian, Indian, and Central Asian styles.
 
• Other architectural marvels built under Akbar’s reign include the Agra Fort and Akbar's Tomb in Sikandra.
 
• Akbar emphasized the integration of different cultures in his architectural projects, symbolizing his policy of religious tolerance.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat Campaign**
 
 
• Akbar’s Gujarat campaign was aimed at consolidating Mughal control over western India.
 
• The victory in Gujarat allowed Akbar to gain control of important trade routes and ports, enhancing the empire’s economic prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Persian Influence in Mughal Architecture**
 
 
• Mughal architecture was significantly influenced by Persian design elements, including domes, arches, and intricate carvings.
 
• The use of red sandstone and marble became prominent under Mughal rule.

questions.question: Who introduced 'Objective Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Objective Resolution' was introduced in the Constituent Assembly of India by **Jawaharlal Nehru** on **13 December 1946**.
 
• This resolution served as a framework and guiding philosophy for the Indian Constitution, outlining the vision for the nation's future.
 
• It stated the principles of sovereignty, equality, justice, liberty, and fraternity to be upheld by the Indian Republic.
 
• The resolution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **22 January 1947**, laying the foundation for drafting the Constitution.
 
• The 'Objective Resolution' eventually evolved into the **Preamble of the Indian Constitution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constituent Assembly of India:**

 
 
• The Constituent Assembly was established in **1946** to draft the Constitution of India.
 
• It comprised representatives elected by provincial assemblies and nominated members.
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad served as the President of the Constituent Assembly.
 
• It functioned until the adoption of the Constitution on **26 November 1949**.
 
 
 
• **Preamble of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• The Preamble enshrines the ideals of **justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity**.
 
• It reflects the vision and philosophy outlined in the 'Objective Resolution'.
 
• The Preamble begins with the phrase, "We, the People of India," signifying democratic principles.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:**
 
 
• He was the first Prime Minister of independent India and a key leader of the Indian independence movement.
 
• Nehru played a pivotal role in shaping India's political and constitutional framework.
 
• He was an advocate for secularism, democracy, and scientific progress in India.
 
 
 
• **Sovereignty in Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Sovereignty implies India's complete independence in making internal and external decisions.
 
• It ensures no external interference in the governance of the nation.
 
• This principle was emphasized in the 'Objective Resolution' and reflected in the Constitution.

questions.question: Raja and Radha Reddy were awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2000 for giving a new dimension to which dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Raja and Radha Reddy** are renowned Indian classical dancers, celebrated for their mastery in the **Kuchipudi dance form**.
 
• They were awarded the **Padma Bhushan** in the year 2000 for their invaluable contribution to Indian classical dance.
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form originating from **Andhra Pradesh**, known for its graceful movements and vibrant expressions.
 
• The duo is credited with giving **a modern dimension** to Kuchipudi while preserving its traditional roots, making it globally recognized.
 
• Their performances often combine **technical precision** with expressive storytelling, showcasing the cultural richness of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi Dance**

 
 
• Kuchipudi is a dance-drama performance art that combines **music, rhythm, and acting**.
 
• It was traditionally performed by male Brahmins, known as **Bhagavathalu**, but is now performed by both genders.
 
• Key features include **Tarangam**, where dancers balance on brass plates while showcasing intricate footwork.
 
• It often depicts stories from Indian mythology, especially from the **Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas**.
 
 
 
• **Padma Bhushan Award**
 
 
• It is India’s **third-highest civilian award**, instituted in 1954.
 
• Awarded for distinguished service of high order across various fields such as arts, literature, science, and public services.
 
• Recipients are selected by a committee constituted by the Prime Minister of India.
 
 
 
• **Raja and Radha Reddy's Legacy**
 
 
• The duo established **Natya Tarangini Institute of Performing Arts** in Delhi to promote Indian classical dance.
 
• They have performed in prestigious venues worldwide, showcasing the beauty of Indian culture.
 
• Through workshops and performances, they have trained numerous students in the Kuchipudi art form.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dance Forms of India**
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam**: Originating from Tamil Nadu, known for fixed upper torso and intricate footwork.
 
• **Odissi**: A dance form from Odisha, characterized by fluid movements and sculpturesque poses.
 
• **Manipuri**: From Manipur, known for its graceful and devotional nature.
 
• **Sattriya**: Originating from Assam, introduced by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardeva.

questions.question: Which of the following options contains groups of cropping seasons in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabi, Kharif and Zaid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **India's cropping seasons** are divided into three major categories: Rabi, Kharif, and Zaid, based on climatic conditions and crop-growing periods.
 
• **Rabi crops** are sown in winter (October-November) and harvested in spring (April-June). Examples include wheat, barley, mustard, and peas.
 
• **Kharif crops** are sown during the monsoon season (June-July) and harvested in autumn (September-October). Examples include paddy, maize, and cotton.
 
• **Zaid crops** are grown in the short season between Rabi and Kharif (March-June). Examples include watermelon, cucumber, and fodder crops.
 
• The classification of these seasons is based on the **Indian climatic cycle** and ensures efficient use of water resources and favorable weather conditions for crop production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabi Crops:**

 
 
• Sowing Period: October-November
 
• Harvesting Period: April-June
 
• Requires cool weather during growth and warm weather during harvesting.
 
• Examples: Wheat, mustard, barley, and gram.
 
 
 
• **Kharif Crops:**
 
 
• Sowing Period: June-July (beginning of monsoon).
 
• Harvesting Period: September-October.
 
• Requires hot weather and high rainfall during growth.
 
• Examples: Rice, maize, cotton, and groundnut.
 
 
 
• **Zaid Crops:**
 
 
• Grown between Rabi and Kharif seasons (March-June).
 
• Requires warm and dry weather with irrigation facilities.
 
• Examples: Watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, and vegetables.
 
 
 
• **Climatic Importance:** These cropping seasons align with India's monsoon cycle, ensuring maximum agricultural productivity by matching sowing and harvesting periods to weather patterns.
 
• **Geographical Relevance:** While these cropping patterns are widely applicable across India, the types of crops grown may vary based on regional soil and climatic conditions.

questions.question: A tunnel that runs through the cell wall between two plant cells is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasmodesmata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plasmodesmata** are microscopic channels that traverse the cell walls of plant cells, establishing a direct connection between the cytoplasm of adjacent cells.
 
• They facilitate **intercellular communication** and the exchange of nutrients, ions, signaling molecules, and other substances.
 
• Plasmodesmata play a critical role in maintaining the **symplastic pathway**, allowing transport of materials through the cytoplasm.
 
• They are formed during **cell division** and remain as permanent structures, enabling plants to function as a cohesive system.
 
• Their structure includes a central **desmotubule** derived from the endoplasmic reticulum, surrounded by cytoplasmic sleeves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Wall**:

 
 
• It is a rigid, protective layer made of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin in plants.
 
• It provides structural support, protection, and regulates cell growth.
 
 
 
• **Symplastic Pathway**:
 
 
• The route of transport of water and solutes through the cytoplasm of cells interconnected by plasmodesmata.
 
• This pathway is crucial for the efficient sharing of resources and signaling across plant tissues.
 
 
 
• **Apoplastic Pathway**:
 
 
• Transport occurs through the cell wall and intercellular spaces without crossing membranes.
 
• It is complementary to the symplastic pathway and is important for water and solute movement.
 
 
 
• **Desmotubule**:
 
 
• A tube-like structure within the plasmodesmata, derived from the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
 
• It helps in maintaining the structure and selective transport of materials between cells.
 
 
 
• **Peroxisomes**:
 
 
• Small organelles found in cells that contain enzymes for metabolic processes, such as breaking down fatty acids and detoxifying hydrogen peroxide.
 
• They are not related to plasmodesmata but are crucial for cellular metabolism.

questions.question: Which state topped the medal tally at the 37th National Games event held in Goa?

questions.question: Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram, who became the first Carnatic musician to win a Grammy, is known for playing which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghatam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram**, also known as "Vikku Vinayakram," is a renowned Carnatic musician and a master of the **Ghatam**.
 
• He is the **first Carnatic musician** to win a Grammy Award, which he received in 1991 for his collaboration on the album "**Planet Drum**" with Mickey Hart.
 
• The **Ghatam** is a traditional South Indian percussion instrument made of clay and is an essential part of Carnatic music performances.
 
• Vikku Vinayakram's innovative techniques and global collaborations have elevated the **Ghatam** to international recognition.
 
• He belongs to a family of musicians and has trained under his father, **T.R. Harihara Sarma**, a renowned percussionist and teacher.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghatam**

 
 
• The Ghatam is a clay pot with a narrow mouth, used as a percussion instrument in South Indian classical music.
 
• It is played with the fingers, palms, and wrists, and the pitch can be modified by pressing the mouth of the pot against the stomach.
 
• The Ghatam is made of a special type of clay mixed with iron filings and baked to achieve its durability and tonal quality.
 
• It is categorized as an idiophone, which produces sound primarily through the vibration of the instrument itself.
 
 
 
• **Grammy Awards**
 
 
• Established in 1959, the Grammy Awards are presented by the Recording Academy to recognize achievements in the music industry.
 
• Vikku Vinayakram received the Grammy in the category of **Best World Music Album** for his contribution to "Planet Drum."
 
 
 
• **Planet Drum**
 
 
• It is an album produced by Mickey Hart, featuring an ensemble of world percussionists.
 
• The album is a celebration of global rhythmic traditions and won the first Grammy in the **World Music** category.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music**
 
 
• Carnatic music is one of the two major traditions of Indian classical music, the other being Hindustani music.
 
• It is characterized by its emphasis on vocal music, intricate compositions, and improvisation.
 
• Instruments like the Ghatam, Mridangam, Veena, and Violin are commonly used in Carnatic music performances.

questions.question: During the Mauryan society, Megasthenes divided the Indian society into seven distinct groups. In which distinct group were the 'king's counsellors' placed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seventh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador in the Mauryan court, classified Indian society into seven distinct groups based on their occupation and societal roles.
 
• The 'king's counsellors' were placed in the **seventh group**, which comprised those responsible for governance and administration.
 
• This classification was primarily documented in Megasthenes' work *Indica*, offering insights into Mauryan societal structure.
 
• The seventh group included not just the king's advisers but also other high-ranking officials and administrators who ensured the effective functioning of the state.
 
• The division emphasized the organizational structure of society under the Mauryan Empire, highlighting the importance of governance roles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Megasthenes:**

 
 
• He was the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus I Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• His work *Indica* provides a detailed account of Indian society, culture, and governance during the Mauryan period.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Empire:**
 
 
• Founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE, it was one of the largest empires in ancient India.
 
• The empire was known for its centralized administration and efficient governance system under rulers like Chandragupta and Ashoka.
 
 
 
• **Seven Groups Classification:**
 
 
• According to Megasthenes, these groups included philosophers, farmers, soldiers, herdsmen, artisans, magistrates, and counselors.
 
• Each group had a distinct role in society, contributing to the economic, military, or administrative strength of the empire.
 
 
 
• **Role of King's Counsellors:**
 
 
• The counsellors played a crucial role in advising the king on governance, policy-making, and administration.
 
• They were considered part of the elite class, holding significant influence in the empire's functioning.

questions.question: How many other members are there in the Finance Commission EXCEPT, Chairman?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Finance Commission of India is composed of **five members in total**: one Chairman and four other members.
 
• The **Chairman** is selected based on their expertise in public affairs, whereas the other four members are chosen for their knowledge in finance, administration, and economics.
 
• The Finance Commission is a **constitutional body** established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The primary role of the Finance Commission is to **recommend the distribution of tax revenues** between the Centre and the States.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India every five years under Article 280 of the Constitution.
 
• It is tasked with recommending measures to improve the financial health of the State and Union governments.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Finance Commission**
 
 
• It determines the **division of net tax proceeds** between the Centre and States.
 
• It recommends the principles to distribute these funds among the states.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications of Members**
 
 
• The members of the Finance Commission must have specialized knowledge in finance, economics, public administration, or governance.
 
 
 
• **Recent Finance Commissions**
 
 
• The **15th Finance Commission**, chaired by N.K. Singh, was constituted in 2017 and submitted its final report for the period 2021-26.
 
• Its recommendations focus on **fiscal consolidation, tax devolution, and grants-in-aid** for the states.

questions.question: Bhangra and Giddha dance forms are associated with which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bhangra and Giddha are traditional dance forms originating from the Indian state of **Punjab**.
 
• **Bhangra** is typically performed by men, showcasing energetic movements to the beat of dhol (a traditional drum).
 
• **Giddha** is a popular folk dance performed by women, characterized by graceful movements and rhythmic clapping.
 
• Both dance forms reflect the **rich cultural heritage of Punjab**, often associated with celebrations such as harvest festivals and weddings.
 
• The vibrancy of these dances represents the **spirit of Punjabi community life and joy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhangra**

 
 
• Originated during the **harvest season**, symbolizing the joy of farmers.
 
• It is now performed globally and has influenced modern music genres like Bollywood and hip-hop.
 
• Traditional Bhangra involves instruments such as dhol, tumbi, and chimta, enhancing its rhythmic beats.
 
 
 
• **Giddha**
 
 
• Performed by women in colorful attire, often accompanied by folk songs known as **boliyan**.
 
• Giddha emphasizes storytelling through dance, with themes ranging from daily life to humor.
 
• It does not rely on musical instruments; instead, performers use clapping to create rhythm.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance**
 
 
• Bhangra and Giddha showcase Punjab's agrarian roots and community traditions.
 
• Both dances are integral to festivals like **Vaisakhi**, which marks the harvest and Sikh New Year.
 
• They are a symbol of unity, joy, and cultural pride for Punjabis worldwide.

questions.question: Which of the following banking institutions played an instrumental role in financial inclusion through microfinance loans and their expansion in India?

options.text: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NABARD** was established in 1982 under a special Act of Parliament to promote rural development and agricultural financing in India.
 
• NABARD has been a pioneer in promoting **financial inclusion** by introducing microfinance initiatives, including the **Self-Help Group (SHG)-Bank Linkage Program**, which empowers rural women and small entrepreneurs.
 
• It has played a critical role in providing **refinancing facilities** to regional rural banks, cooperative banks, and other financial institutions to expand credit access in rural areas.
 
• Through its support for microfinance institutions (MFIs), NABARD has enabled millions of low-income households in rural India to access small loans for livelihood enhancement and entrepreneurship.
 
• NABARD also focuses on capacity building and rural infrastructure development, ensuring a sustainable and inclusive financial ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Help Group (SHG)-Bank Linkage Program**

 
 
• Launched by NABARD in 1992, this program is the largest microfinance initiative in the world.
 
• It encourages rural households to form groups, save collectively, and access credit from formal financial institutions.
 
• It has significantly empowered women and improved livelihoods in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance**
 
 
• Microfinance refers to providing small loans and other financial services to low-income individuals or groups who lack access to traditional banking services.
 
• It helps in promoting entrepreneurship, reducing poverty, and fostering financial inclusion.
 
 
 
• **Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF)**
 
 
• Established by NABARD in 1995-96, RIDF funds infrastructure projects in rural areas, such as roads, irrigation, and healthcare facilities.
 
• It aims to enhance rural productivity and quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion**
 
 
• Financial inclusion is the process of ensuring access to financial services like credit, savings, insurance, and payments for all, particularly marginalized and low-income groups.
 
• Institutions like NABARD, RBI, and others work to bridge the gap in financial access for rural and underserved populations.

questions.question: Deodhar Trophy is given in _______.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• **Deodhar Trophy** is a domestic cricket tournament in India organized by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).
 
• It is named after the legendary Indian cricketer, **Prof. D.B. Deodhar**, who is often referred to as the "Father of Indian Cricket."

• Initially, the format featured zonal teams (North Zone, South Zone, East Zone, West Zone, and Central Zone), but later evolved into a three-team competition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Domestic Cricket Tournaments in India:**

 
 
• **Ranji Trophy:** India's premier first-class cricket tournament introduced in 1934.
 
• **Irani Cup:** Played between the Ranji Trophy winners and the Rest of India team.
 
• **Vijay Hazare Trophy:** A domestic one-day cricket championship launched in 2002-03.
 
• **Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy:** A domestic T20 competition started in 2006-07.
 
 
 
• **Key Players:** The Deodhar Trophy has been instrumental in highlighting future stars of Indian cricket, such as **Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma, and Shubman Gill**.
 
• **Format:** Matches are played in a one-day format with 50 overs per side, following standard ICC regulations.
 
• **Significance:** The tournament provides opportunities for domestic players to showcase their skills and earn selection for the Indian national team.

questions.question: The elements in Group 17 of the periodic table are known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Halogens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The elements in Group 17 of the periodic table are called **Halogens**, derived from the Greek words "halos" (salt) and "gen" (to produce), meaning "salt producers."
 
• Halogens include five elements: **Fluorine (F), Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I), and Astatine (At)**.
 
• These elements are highly reactive nonmetals and are known for forming **salts** when they react with metals.
 
• Halogens have seven valence electrons, making them one electron short of a stable octet configuration, which accounts for their high reactivity.
 
• The chemical reactivity of halogens decreases down the group: **Fluorine > Chlorine > Bromine > Iodine > Astatine**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Physical Properties:**

 
 
• Halogens exist in all three states of matter at room temperature: Fluorine and Chlorine (gases), Bromine (liquid), and Iodine/Astatine (solids).
 
• Their melting and boiling points increase down the group due to stronger van der Waals forces.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Fluorine is used in toothpaste (as fluoride) and Teflon production.
 
• Chlorine is used as a disinfectant and in the production of PVC (polyvinyl chloride).
 
• Bromine is used in flame retardants, while Iodine is vital for thyroid health.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity with Hydrogen:**
 
 
• Halogens react with hydrogen to form hydrogen halides (e.g., HF, HCl), which dissolve in water to form strong acids.
 
 
 
• **Occurrence:**
 
 
• Halogens are not found in their elemental state in nature due to their high reactivity but occur as halide ions in various compounds.
 
 
 
• **Trends in Group 17:**
 
 
• Electronegativity decreases down the group, with Fluorine being the most electronegative element in the periodic table.
 
• Oxidizing power decreases from Fluorine to Iodine.

questions.question: Who among the following married the Mughal emperor Jahangir in 1611 and received the title 'Nur Jahan'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mehrunnisa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mehrunnisa**, later known as **Nur Jahan**, married Emperor Jahangir in 1611 and became his twentieth and most beloved wife.
 
• Nur Jahan, meaning "Light of the World," was a title conferred upon Mehrunnisa by Jahangir after their marriage.
 
• She became an influential figure in the Mughal court, wielding significant political power and even issuing royal orders (farmans) under her own name.
 
• Mehrunnisa was the daughter of Mirza Ghiyas Beg, a Persian noble, and she played a critical role in the cultural and administrative developments of the Mughal Empire.
 
• Her marriage to Jahangir marked her rise as one of the most powerful women in Mughal history, deeply involved in state affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nur Jahan's Political Influence:**

 
 
• She was actively involved in governance and is known to have participated in the imperial administration alongside Jahangir.
 
• Her name was inscribed on coins, a significant marker of her authority and influence.
 
 
 
• **Contribution to Mughal Art and Culture:**
 
 
• Nur Jahan was a patron of architecture, poetry, and the arts, commissioning several gardens and monuments.
 
• One of her most famous contributions was the design of the Itimad-ud-Daulah's Tomb in Agra, often referred to as the "Baby Taj."
 
 
 
• **Background of Mehrunnisa:**
 
 
• Mehrunnisa was born in 1577 in Kandahar, present-day Afghanistan, and her family migrated to India seeking fortune in the Mughal court.
 
• Before marrying Jahangir, she was previously married to Sher Afghan, a Mughal officer, who died under disputed circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Nur Jahan remains one of the most iconic and influential women in Mughal history, symbolizing power and elegance.
 
• Her life and achievements continue to inspire historical and literary works, showcasing her as a strong figure in a predominantly male-dominated era.

questions.question: What solution should be used to test for the presence of starch in food?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Iodine solution** is commonly used to test for the presence of starch in food items.
 
• When iodine solution is applied to a substance containing starch, it reacts to form a **blue-black color**, indicating the presence of starch.
 
• The reaction occurs because iodine molecules interact with the helical structure of amylose, a component of starch.
 
• This test is highly specific to starch and does not produce similar reactions with other carbohydrates like glucose or sucrose.
 
• Iodine solution is prepared by dissolving iodine in potassium iodide and water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Starch:**

 
 
• Starch is a polysaccharide composed of glucose units linked together, commonly found in plants.
 
• It is a major source of energy in the human diet, present in foods like potatoes, rice, and wheat.
 
 
 
• **Amylose and Amylopectin:**
 
 
• Starch consists of two components: **amylose** (linear chains) and **amylopectin** (branched chains).
 
• The iodine solution primarily reacts with amylose to produce the blue-black coloration.
 
 
 
• **Iodine Solution Preparation:**
 
 
• Iodine solution is created by dissolving iodine crystals in a potassium iodide solution, which increases iodine's solubility in water.
 
• It is often diluted before use in laboratory experiments.
 
 
 
• **Other Applications of Iodine Solution:**
 
 
• Besides starch testing, iodine solution is used as a disinfectant and antiseptic in medical applications.
 
• It is also employed in titration experiments to determine the concentration of substances in chemistry.

questions.question: Which of the following ministries has launched the National Career Service Portal (www.ncs.gov.in) ?

options.text: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Labour and Employment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Career Service Portal (**www.ncs.gov.in**) was launched by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** in **July 2015** to connect job seekers with employers.
 
• It is a one-stop platform aimed at providing **employment-related services**, including job postings, career counseling, skill training, and placement assistance.
 
• The portal offers services to **students, job seekers, employers, skill providers, career counselors**, and placement organizations.
 
• The initiative is part of the government's mission to provide **transparent, efficient, and accessible employment services** to the citizens of India.
 
• The NCS Portal is integrated with **Aadhaar** for verification purposes and facilitates real-time job matching based on user profiles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Career Service (NCS)**

 
 
• It was launched under the **National Career Service Project**, which is an initiative of the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
 
• The project aims to modernize the existing **National Employment Service** by leveraging technology to provide efficient and user-friendly services.
 
• The portal provides **free registration and services** for all Indian citizens, ensuring inclusivity and accessibility.
 
• The service also facilitates **career guidance and counseling** through a network of Model Career Centers (MCCs) across the country.
 
 
 
• **Employment Exchanges**
 
 
• Before the NCS Portal, employment exchanges were the primary mechanism for job matching in India.
 
• These exchanges operated manually, which resulted in inefficiencies and limited outreach.
 
• The NCS Portal modernized this approach by digitizing job-matching services and providing real-time data accessibility.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Employment Generation**
 
 
• **Skill India Mission:** Focuses on providing skill training to the youth to enhance employability.
 
• **Make in India:** Aims to boost manufacturing and create job opportunities in India.
 
• **Startup India:** Promotes entrepreneurship and supports startups with financial and regulatory assistance.
 
• **PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana:** Provides free skill training to increase employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Aadhaar Integration**
 
 
• Aadhaar integration ensures **identity verification** and prevents duplication of job seeker profiles.
 
• It enhances the credibility and transparency of the services provided by the portal.

questions.question: As per Census 2011, which of the following union territories has the highest percentage of rural population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per Census 2011, **Puducherry** has the highest percentage of rural population among all Union Territories in India.
 
• The rural population of Puducherry constitutes **31.5%** of its total population, which is significantly higher compared to other Union Territories.
 
• In contrast, Union Territories like Delhi and Chandigarh are predominantly urban with negligible rural populations.
 
• Puducherry's rural areas are primarily located in the districts of Karaikal, Yanam, and Mahe, which contribute to its higher rural population percentage.
 
• Other Union Territories such as Daman and Diu and Lakshadweep have lower rural population percentages due to their smaller geographical areas and urban-centric development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census 2011:**

 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years and provides detailed demographic, social, and economic data of the country.
 
• Census 2011 was the 15th Census of India and marked the second census of the 21st century.
 
• It recorded India's total population as 1.21 billion, with 68.84% residing in rural areas and 31.16% in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Union Territories of India:**
 
 
• As of 2021, India has 8 Union Territories, including Delhi, Chandigarh, Puducherry, and others.
 
• Union Territories are directly governed by the Central Government of India, unlike states that have their own governments.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization Trends in India:**
 
 
• India has been witnessing a steady rise in urbanization, with urban areas expanding due to migration and infrastructure development.
 
• However, rural regions still account for a significant portion of the population, especially in states and certain Union Territories like Puducherry.
 
 
 
• **Rural Development in Puducherry:**
 
 
• Puducherry's rural areas are known for agriculture, fishing, and traditional industries.
 
• The government has initiated several rural development schemes to improve infrastructure, livelihoods, and living standards in these regions.

questions.question: On which of the following days is National Integration Day observed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**19 November.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National Integration Day in India is observed on **November 19** every year.
 
• This day marks the birth anniversary of **Indira Gandhi**, the first female Prime Minister of India.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of **unity, peace, and harmony among all citizens** of the country.
 
• Various activities such as seminars, cultural programs, and discussions are organized across schools and institutions to promote the message of national integration.
 
• It is a day dedicated to fostering **social cohesion** and eradicating discrimination based on religion, caste, or region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indira Gandhi's Contributions:**

 
 
• Indira Gandhi served as the Prime Minister of India from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 until her assassination in 1984.
 
• She played a significant role in shaping India's foreign policy and initiated the **Green Revolution** to boost agricultural productivity.
 
• She was instrumental in the liberation of Bangladesh during the **1971 Indo-Pak war**.
 
 
 
• **National Integration:**
 
 
• National integration refers to the process of creating a sense of unity and solidarity among citizens of a country, regardless of cultural, religious, or regional differences.
 
• It aims to strengthen the bond of brotherhood and promote equitable development across diverse communities.
 
 
 
• **Other Observances on November 19:**
 
 
• November 19 is also celebrated as **World Toilet Day**, highlighting the importance of sanitation and hygiene globally.
 
• It is a day to reflect on the efforts needed to achieve sustainable and equitable sanitation for all.
 
 
 
• **Famous Quotes by Indira Gandhi:**
 
 
• "You cannot shake hands with a clenched fist."
 
• "The power to question is the basis of all human progress."
 
• These quotes encapsulate her philosophy of peace, progress, and unity.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a tributary of Godavari River?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kameng**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Godavari River is the second-longest river in India and originates from Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra.
 
• Important tributaries of the Godavari River include **Indravati, Pranhita, Manjira, Sabari, and Purna**.
 
• **Kameng River** is not a tributary of the Godavari; it flows in the northeastern region of India and is a tributary of the Brahmaputra River.
 
• Kameng River originates in the Tawang district of Arunachal Pradesh and flows through the Assam region to join the Brahmaputra.
 
• The Godavari River basin covers states like Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Godavari River:**

 
 
• Known as the "Dakshin Ganga" or "Ganga of the South" due to its importance in southern India.
 
• Total length: ~1,465 km, making it the longest river in peninsular India.
 
• The river supports irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric projects in the region.
 
• It flows into the Bay of Bengal, forming a large delta in Andhra Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Kameng River:**
 
 
• It is a major tributary of the Brahmaputra River, flowing in northeastern India.
 
• Originates at the glacier near the Gorichen Peak in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The river is known for its pristine beauty and biodiversity.
 
• It is a vital water source for wildlife sanctuaries like Pakke Tiger Reserve.
 
 
 
• **Tributaries:**
 
 
• A tributary is a smaller river or stream that flows into a larger river or main water body.
 
• Tributaries play a critical role in the hydrology and ecosystem of the main river.
 
• The term “left-bank” or “right-bank” tributary is used depending on the direction of inflow.
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra River:**
 
 
• One of the major rivers of Asia, originating in Tibet and flowing into India and Bangladesh.
 
• It is known for its high sediment content and annual flooding during the monsoon season.
 
• The Brahmaputra basin is rich in biodiversity and supports millions of people with agriculture and fishing.

questions.question: Who among the following are the target beneficiaries for the 'Vishwakarma Yojana' launched by Government of India on 17 September 2023?

options.text: Individuals skilled in traditional folk dance
Individuals skilled in traditional folk songs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Individuals skilled in traditional craftsmanship**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Vishwakarma Yojana was launched by the Government of India on **17 September 2023**, coinciding with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's birthday.
 
• The scheme targets individuals engaged in **traditional craftsmanship and artisanal trades** to promote their skills and livelihoods.
 
• It is aimed at providing financial assistance, skill development, and modern tools to artisans such as carpenters, blacksmiths, cobblers, masons, goldsmiths, potters, and others.
 
• The scheme seeks to **preserve and promote India's rich heritage of craftsmanship** while boosting self-reliance and economic growth among skilled workers.
 
• The beneficiaries of the Vishwakarma Yojana will receive support to enhance their productivity and integrate their skills into the mainstream economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Traditional Craftsmanship in India**

 
 
• India is known for its diverse traditional arts and crafts, including weaving, pottery, metalworking, and wood carving.
 
• Craftsmanship has historically been a major source of livelihood for millions of skilled workers across rural and urban areas.
 
• Many traditional artisans face challenges such as lack of modern tools, limited market access, and insufficient financial support.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of Vishwakarma Yojana**
 
 
• To uplift traditional artisans by offering comprehensive financial aid and skill training.
 
• To preserve India's rich cultural heritage by supporting individuals skilled in traditional craftsmanship.
 
• To integrate artisan trades into India's modern economy by enhancing their productivity and market reach.
 
 
 
• **Skill Development Initiatives**
 
 
• Under Vishwakarma Yojana, beneficiaries will undergo training programs to upgrade their skills and adapt to new technologies.
 
• The government plans to provide modern tools and equipment to artisans for improving efficiency and output.
 
 
 
• **Government's Focus on Self-Reliance**
 
 
• The scheme aligns with India's broader vision of "Atmanirbhar Bharat" (Self-Reliant India).
 
• By empowering traditional artisans, the government aims to bolster economic growth and reduce dependence on imports in the handicraft and artisanal sectors.
